About Root Cause

Answers before assumptions.

Root Cause LLC was founded in 2026 by ISA Certified Arborist Kristy Garland. After more than 10 years working in arboriculture and plant health care, Kristy recognized an important need: property owners deserve to know what is happening to their trees and plants, why it is happening, and what can realistically be done to correct or manage the problem.

Kristy holds a degree in horticulture and brings extensive hands-on experience in tree and plant diagnostics. Root Cause examines the full picture, explains the findings in understandable terms, and recommends practical options for correction, treatment, monitoring, further testing, or replacement.

Kristy is also a Wisconsin-certified and licensed commercial pesticide applicator. Root Cause LLC holds a Wisconsin Commercial Pesticide Application Business License, allowing professional plant-health treatments when they are appropriate.

No plant is too big or too small. She loves them all.

How Root Cause can help

Care based on the actual problem.

Symptoms may come from insects, disease, planting mistakes, roots, soil, weather, watering, construction, or several factors working together.

01

Tree & Plant Diagnostics

Evaluation of decline, discoloration, dieback, unusual growth, and loss of vigor.

02

Root & Planting Problems

Planting depth, buried root flares, girdling roots, mulch, soil, and root-zone stress.

03

Insect & Disease Management

Identification, monitoring, and treatment recommendations when action is warranted.

04

Plant Health Care

Fertilization, soil and root-zone care, trunk injections, and practical care plans.

The clues matter

What you see is only the beginning.

A thinning plant tells us where to start. A closer inspection of needles, buds, twigs, bark, roots, and site conditions helps narrow down why it is happening.

Correcting the cause

The problem was underground.

This tree had been planted incorrectly by landscapers. These photographs show the investigation and corrective process as the buried root flare and structural roots were uncovered.

Good tree care often begins below the surface.
